title: Rome makes the Church a superior revelation that proves Scripture
source_text: XXIII. At vero Pontificii nolunt Scripturam sacram immediate et per se fidem apud nos mereri et obtinere; sed docent esse aliam divinam revelationem per quam Scripturam probari necesse sit, ut publice de ea in Ecclesia constet. Et haec revelatio ipsis est Ecclesiae vox et testimonium, hoc est praepositorum Ecclesiae doctrina. Siquidem Deum ipsum per Ecclesiae pastores hodie loqui volunt, tanquam per organa, quoad fidei doctrinam, infallibilia, quemadmodum olim locutus est per Prophetas atque Apostolos. Itaque admittunt quidem Scripturam esse fidei regulam, sed subalternam atque partialem, quae superiori et ampliori regula probari indigeat. Quapropter ad fidei dogmata comprobanda afferunt quidem Scripturae sacrae authoritatem. Sed si rogentur cur sacrae Scripturae fidem adhibeant, dicunt se id facere propter Ecclesiae suae testimonium, et in hoc testimonio, tanquam inter fidei externa principia supremo, conquiescere ipsos necesse est, si quidem suis placitis stare velint. Nos quidem ad libri alicujus sacri authoritatem comprobandam afferimus quoque constans Ecclesiae testimonium: verum non sicut ipsi, tanquam aliquod fidei principium cui fides nostra subjicienda sit: sed solum tanquam quoddam argumentum a posteriori, validum quidem et bonum, sed non prorsus divinum atque infallibile.
pass_a_gloss: But the Pontificii refuse to have sacred Scripture deserve and obtain faith among us immediately and of itself; they teach that there is another divine revelation through which Scripture must be proved, so that it may be publicly established concerning it in the Church. And this revelation for them is the Church's voice and testimony — that is, the doctrine of the Church's overseers. For they want God himself to speak today through the Church's pastors as through organs infallible as to the doctrine of faith, just as he once spoke through the Prophets and Apostles. So they do admit that Scripture is a rule of faith, but a subordinate and partial one that needs to be proved by a superior and fuller rule. Therefore for proving dogmas of faith they do bring in sacred Scripture's authority. But if they are asked why they give faith to sacred Scripture, they say they do it because of their Church's testimony, and in that testimony — as the supreme among external principles of faith — they must rest if they wish to stand by their own teachings. We too, for proving some sacred book's authority, bring forward the Church's constant testimony: yet not as they do, as some principle of faith to which our faith must be subjected, but only as a certain argument from the later effect — valid and good, yet not wholly divine and infallible.
pass_b_english: The Pontificii will not let sacred Scripture deserve and win our faith immediately and of itself. They teach another divine revelation by which Scripture must be proved, so that the Church may publicly settle its standing. For them that revelation is the Church's voice and testimony — the doctrine of her overseers. They want God to speak today through the Church's pastors as through organs infallible in the doctrine of faith, as he once spoke through Prophets and Apostles.

So they admit Scripture is a rule of faith, yet a subordinate and partial one that needs proving by a superior, fuller rule. When they prove dogmas they do cite sacred Scripture's authority. Asked why they trust sacred Scripture, they say: because of their Church's testimony — and in that testimony, as the supreme external principle of faith, they must rest if they mean to keep their own teachings.

We too bring the Church's constant testimony when we prove a sacred book's authority. But not as they do — not as a principle of faith to which our faith must be subjected. For us it is only an argument from the later effect: sound and strong, yet not wholly divine and infallible.

choices.why: Readable English for Rome's lesser rule under a superior one.
Glosses the technical tag so Pass B stays plain.
